questions.stem: Why do addition reactions always have 100% atom economy?

options.text: Because they always have a 100% percentage yield
Because all atoms from the reactants end up in a single product with no by-products
Because they only use one reactant
Because they always occur at high temperatures

questions.explanation: In an addition reaction, all atoms from the reactants are incorporated into a single product. There are no by-products, so no atoms are wasted. This gives an atom economy of 100%. Note that atom economy is different from percentage yield — a reaction can have 100% atom economy but less than 100% yield.
